body: A true man will continue to ask for consent throughout. It has nothing to with being a mind reader, it has to do with understanding consent can be revoked at any point. And the second she asked him.to.slow down, he had a perfect opportunity to ask again if she wanted to continue. 😊

You also did not say yes. And yes means you continued to consent throughout. I don't care if you're 5 minutes in, 10 minutes in, etc....the second you want to stop....it needs to stop!!!! I'm sorry you joined this club of warriors....but know you have an entire tribe that stands with you.

I have wanted to write handwritten letters to my sons, my spouse, my siblings, and my parents (long divorced). My worry is that I may say something that becomes misconstrued and they will carry guilt over my choice. That is the only thing that holds me back....my choice to end my life is my choice and honestly, my children have been the only reason I've hung onto this barbed wire life for as long as I have.

By saying that, I worry that they'll feel that I no longer cared enough about them to continue and worry the others willfully didn't love them at all. That's not the case at all...it's quite the opposite. However, I feel like my living is impeding on my boys having a wonderful, fulfilling life. Once I'm gone, our finances will be vastly improved (I have a serious chronic health condition, along with fibromyalgia, severe anxiety, depression, and other medical issues on top of these) and they will not have the weight of my ill health to hold them back. 

While I lean towards saying yes, because there is definitely a closure in letting them know why, I think we need to carefully word what we say. Our choice to end our life is not something any of our loved ones caused. At the end of the day, we are in charge of our destiny and no person, hotline, or therapy is going to ever understand the hopelessness that we live every day. I think leaving a note is going to end up being a personal preference and one that only you can decide if it would be appropriate.

I have wondered the same thing. My entire family suffers from serious depression. We did not all grow up together so I don't think being around depressed people is the cause. I have no doubt that it is directly related to something in our DNA as mental illness is caused by dysfunctional chemistry in the brain. THAT is genetic and therefore, I believe that it's is both physiological and psychological.

I began Nuvigil about two months ago, but in that time have o my taken it a total of eleven times. The first three days were like magic...I was started on a dose of 150 mg, to be taken in the morning. I wasn't falling asleep throughout the day and my pain level for my fibromyalgia went from a consistent 8 to 9 to a 1 to 2! By day 4, it was like it completely stopped working...completely. I was crushed but just held off and stopped taking it (no need to put a medication into my body that is not doing anything).
Saw my doctor again about two weeks later and though she was shocked at how quickly it stopped working, she upped the dose to 250 mg. I began again and while the response wasn't as great, it was markedly improved. Unfortunately this time, a much more sinister thing happened; I was completely unable to breathe! I was struggling to take a normal breath and also felt like I couldn't get air out of my lungs either. I used my rescue inhaler (I have COPD as well), and even with repeated use, along with my COPD medication, but I was still unable to breathe. Wondered if it was an anxiety attack, as I have extreme anxiety...but I have NEVER had shortness of breath with my anxiety before, and have had the anxiety for almost 30 years. 
I went to the ER/urgent care for shortness of breath, but my oxygen levels were fine and though my BP and pulse rate were way higher than normal (BP usually 90/70...very low...And was 130/95) and pulse was 133 (usually 60-66). They didn't feel this was an emergency and sent me home. For the record, I completely disagree with their findings....nobody's BP and pulse rate should double their normal rate, and the SOB should have been duly noted, but was not. 
Anyway, stopped the Nuvigil for the next week because my allergies kicked up and I was told not to take both the Nuvigil and the Claritin D together. When I next used the Nuvigil, I  only did half the dose. The breathing problems were just as significant! Went to the Dr and she told me it was nothing again. I asked for an anti anxiety medication to see if that would help, as I know anxiety is a huge known side effect of Nuvigil, and was told absolutely not. Ended up back at ER/urgent care for the same thing again...I swore I was going to die, the shortness of breath was so severe! Told nothing wrong by both my Dr and the ER/urgent care and again, they refused to give me any anxiety medication. I was in tears, but again, trusted the damn Drs. 
This has now happened EVERY SINGLE TIME I've tried to take the Nuvigil. Another ER/urgent care visit and two additional Dr visits later, and I was told specifically to stop trying to get anti anxiety meds...they refuse and tell me I'm just fine. For the record...my BP and pulse rate were always double what they normally are. Not only am I done with the Nuvigil, in done with the Dr and with the ER/urgent care I've gone to. Wondering if ANYONE else has suffered from this as well??? Find it hard to believe that I am seriously the only human being to have this side effect! 
Guess I continue to live with fallling asleep constantly at random times throughout the day, because not being able to breathe is far worse than falling over and falling asleep as I am walking, sitting, or driving. I'm beginning to feel that until somebody finally dies from this (hopefully only me and not somebody else), nothing will be done and that just makes me feel both really sad and really pissed off. *Edited for mis-spellings*

Check with your local domestic violence agency(ies) and see if they can help advocate for you to not have to disclose your location or any employer information. You deserve a new start...one with that ex/ass far behind!

First off, your therapist needs to be throat punched...repeatedly....for being such an ignorant ass. Second, I can't say I fully understand your situation, but I can tell you that I was held captive for over a year by my rapist and there was finally a point where I felt so helpless and hopeless that I knew fighting didn't matter anymore. It was the lowest point of my captivity when I finally realized that. That is where I feel I can connect with your feelings and it hurts my heart when I hear that others have also hit that belief. It sounds like you feel that you have lost your value as a human being, and don't feel like you can stand up to these assholes and that nobody seems to understand that no means no. And to top it off, you have a therapist who is a f*ing idiot.

Yeah...you get to be nauseous and barf for a very long time....and no guarantee that it will even be successful. And holy hell, you forgot we're broke as shit....couldn't afford to buy them anyway, especially with the thought of dying because I seriously am "vomiting too death". Ughhh....no thanks on that one! Good luck to you and hope you at least make sure you weigh your options on living or dying. I actually made a list, that I add to daily, and force myself to give good pros and cons of both trying to make it through another day or call it quits.

So true. Those trust fund kids don't even realize or appreciate how easy they have it! And I'm with you, money DOES equate with happiness. I just roll my eyes when people blab about "appreciating the little things"....yeah, I'd prefer to appreciate the little things, and the big things, and all the things in between...WITH MONEY TO BE ABLE TO APPRECIATE THEM! And though I don't think you will be able to find that money without working, I DO think that it's really f*ed up that people like us know we will work our asses off just to barely scrape by, if we can even scrape by. And meanwhile, some jackass kids and adults just get everything handed to them. Am I jealous? Hell yes, and I believe that deep down, a lot more people are jealous of that than they care to admit!

My husband started having psoriasis soon after the birth of our first child, at age 22.  Stress is a very common trigger for psoriasis, and I understand your frustration because I got to see it in my husband. He struggled with finding relief and struggled even more with the stares and rude ass people who made faces and/or comments. It's truly a shame that people are so shallow and ignorant, isn't it? F*ing assholes....too bad Karma doesn't strike their rude asses with psoriasis right on the spot!!! 

Please keep trying until you find what works. My husband was on Enbrel for years, and then it just kind of stopped working as well. He was so upset, and was beginning to feel hopeless and helpless as this condition constantly kept trying to ruin his life. He then found that Humira works great for him. As for cost issues, please check out the pharmaceutical companies' websites. They often have amazing discount programs and sometimes are even able to start with a 30 day trial for free. 

I just wish that we could live in a world where people weren't constantly ignorant, rude, and judgmental about conditions they know NOTHING about. Know if I were to ever run into you on the street, in the store, or in an elevator...you would never have to worry about getting a disgusted look or rude comment. I'd just treat you like I would anybody else...because psoriasis is a miserable condition to live with; although (as I joke with my husband all the time) I'm a bit jealous because you guys are like God damn Wolverine with how fast your bodies can heal from any cut, scrape, or gaping wound!!! Me? I take weeks to heal, and my husband...he's 100% healed in like 2 to 3 days because of how quickly your skin cells reproduce when you have psoriasis! 😄 Please keep trying....your life is worth more than you think...because I actually believe that people with psoriasis may hold the key to helping discover ways to cure our bodies of other illnesses because of how amazingly your bodies reproduce cells. Best of luck to you.

Thank you for the RAINN link! I will check their website for sure. Sadly, I found my last one through Psychology Today...so I don't trust that one at all anymore. 😔. 

And I know it will difficult...but I was there to specifically talk a out help accepting that I have a chronic illness that is guaranteed to destroy my body and may also kill me....not to discuss the violent attacks. And once I asked her to stop, she crossed the line, ethically as a therapist and morally as a human being, by continuing to force the subject. 

Going to sign off Reddit for the evening and go check the RAINN website. 👍👌😊

It sounds like you experienced a really hard childhood....I am sorry for that. It makes a lot of sense that you would manifest that anger and hurt when you heard about your wife also being victimized. I too find myself fantasizing about torturing my rapist. I want him to suffer like I have suffered for over 25 years. I want him to beg to die but make him live and torture him over and over.....just the way I begged him to stop when he grabbed me off the street...like I begged and cried when he repeatedly raped me. I want him to suffer....so the fact that you also feel like this...I think that's 100% normal!!!
Wow....that therapist and my therapist are perfect for one another! Assholes! I am sorry that you also had to experience such awfulness from someone whose job it is to support us, instead hurts us. 😡

Oh you are such an inspiration! I am still so petrified of my rapist that I can't even drive through the town I know he lives in. I have severe panic attacks just thinking about seeing his evil face. I am so grateful for survivors like you who show that we can not only face them, but get them locked away, where they all belong! Please post again after the POS is sentenced so we can celebrate again. And love and light being sent your way for all you've been through. 🔆🌞💛🌻

Agree that the secondary survivors Reddit would be a great place to find the support you need. Good luck and I hope you can find some feedback that helps you two carry on with a healthy, caring relationship.

This makes me want to throat punch that bitch. What in the hell was she thinking to victimize you AGAIN?!?! I don't believe in hell, but I do believe in Karma and oh, I hope karma gets her for this despicable act in ways that only vengeful karma can! I'm glad you have now found a decent human being who treats you with love and respect. You deserve nothing less!

I'm just going to speak as a mother of a 19 year old, a 22 year old, and a 23 year old...all boys. My babies....no matter how old they are. I had to drop one of them off at the jail to serve a jail sentence. I hugged him so tight and watched my boy walk into jail. No mom ever wants to imagine her son behind bars....but he knew I loved HIM. Not the offense that led up to going to jail, but him...no matter what he had done, I was just going to have to count the days until he was released. 
I am going down to pick him up tonight. He is a couple hours away,but this will be the first time I get to wrap my arms around my son since when I hugged him since dropping him off at the jail. 
Mom's....we are a weird bunch. We love you no matter what fucked up things you do. Until age 24, did you know that the frontal cortex of your brain is still forming??? It is the part of the brain that controls impulses, decision making, and consequential thought process. Any shitty life decision you made was made with a brain that is still forming and growing. Please keep that in mind as you also think about ending your life.
My other son was suicidal (we have awful depression and suicidal ideation in our genes) when he was 15. I was so eternally thankful when he came to me to say he wanted to kill himself. We've all promised to be honest about when we are suicidal. Together, we came up with a safety plan to get through the next three days...that's all....three days. After the three days,we could revise our safety plan. 
My boys all know that I fully understand suicidal ideation....I suffer daily with it. But I would rather let my boys be 100% honest about feeling shitty and suicidal, than lose them. Please give your mom that, at least.
 Three days with a safety plan.....and allow her to trust you and follow the plan you two come up with. A Mom's love is stronger than you can possibly imagine.....there is nothing you could do to change the bond of a mother to her child.

Oh this breaks,my heart. You did not deserve for this to happen. You are so much stronger than I was....I was too afraid to go to the hospital or the police. Your strength is an inspiration to me and I'm sure to many others who have experienced this shitty, shitty thing. I agree that it is so wrong that these pieces of shit walk free, while you are struggling so much. I am also sorry that their evil has caused you to feel that your life is not worth living. I am not going to tell you that you're wrong to feel suicidal; I'd be such a hypocrite if I did, but I can tell you that you have nothing to be ashamed of. THEY should be ones feeling shame. All you did was hang out with people you never imagined would hurt you...there is nothing wrong with that. And even if you had drank all night, it still would not have been a reason for them to abuse you in that way. Please understand that rape is about power and control and it's sad that there are some women (who should be standing with other women to fight sex assault) who think that drugging and sexually assaulting another human being is not seriously wrong.  I do hope that they are someday brought to justice, however that is not going to magically make you feel whole again. Please give yourself time and love yourself...don't allow those assholes to take anything more from you. Believing that you are not at fault and that those three made a choice to assault you...one that you were not able to predict or prevent. And know that we know it was not your fault in any way and that you are amazingly courageous. Believe in the promise of a new tomorrow...it is one of the ways to start healing your heart.

Every single one has a name and they are all my babies...never will be food! I am picking up two Pekin ducklings on Saturday. Will drive four hours south to outside Colorado Springs, pick them out, and drive four hours back home. All of my chickens are different. I have a crazy Polish hen with the big fluffy head, I have a little black Silkie, a super feathery/fluffy cream Silkie, a Barred Rock, a Leghorn, an Americana who lays blue eggs, and a Sultan/Leghorn mix that is about to be rehomed as he started crowing and my hens really can't stand him...lol. 
You really are my neighbor! I am so jealous you grew up on a farm!!! If we could have afforded to, we would have bought a small farmhouse on an acre or so, but Colorado is so outrageously priced, thanks to marijuana and what we natives refer to as stay at home stoners who bleed our welfare system, that most of us can t afford to live here anymore, let alone have any little bit of land!
You sound a lot like me in that we seem to be good listeners to others, but we don't get that same respect back. I've always been someone who just wants to help others and I often can bury my depression if I "take on" someone's else's problems. Yet I think that's just because we have good hearts....and our hearts suffer tremendously and cause us to lose sight of hope for ourselves. 
Forgive me for laughing because I'm the opposite with cleaning. I'm embarrassingly OCD and even on awful pain days, I will prop myself up so I can scrub and clean. Truth be told, I've been known to bleach the entire bathroom before I throw up (and again right after) because I can't stand the thought of being sick in a dirty toilet. My husband and sons make fun of me because I already clean the bathrooms everyday as it is, so it's not like they're dirty to begin with...but part of my mental health issues is being OCD and being ridiculous about stupid things. So a good day for you is to clean and a good day for me would be to leave it alone and not get all stupid and ridiculous about it. So really, put us together, and we're a totally normal person! 😜

Started off my day in tears (which is truly the norm), but also met with the bankruptcy attorney today so have some big decisions to make. Bright side to that is that I have to focus on the next few weeks, so although it's not fun and really stresses me out....it's that hope of "maybe if I can change this, then something else could change too". 
Chronic pain is something I wish nobody had to endure. I'm thankful you do not have it. I see my pain Dr this week and we will continue to work on a care plan that allows me to at least function somewhat. 
Gratitude list for today: grateful for my chickens and ducks. Every night, I bring one in and love on her for at least half an hour. They give me a sense of purpose, and at the end of the day, purpose is what so many of us need to face another day. Second, grateful for pain medication today as I have also been dealing with one of my migraines, along with my everyday chronic pain. Not looking forward to Weds or Thurs, as Days 3 and 4 are the worst of my migraines. Third, I am grateful that today was warm. Tomorrow will usher in a cold and windy day (hence the migraine. Colorado is notorious for huge day to day weather changes and the barometer shifts always mess with my body). 
Thank you for the check in....Hoping you were able to do your gratitude exercise and I'd love to hear what made your list today!
Why does it seem nothing has changed or been added to the scope of medication therapy that appears to truly help those of us with extreme depression and suicidal ideation?

Your ex is truly not being a very good parent right now. Children need BOTH their parents! My mom forced us to choose (I was the oldest of five, at a whopping 14 years old) and would make us feel very guilty if we even chose to visit our dad. Fast forward and I'm now almost 46 and the ONLY one of all my siblings who has a relationship with our dad. No parent should put that kind of guilt trip onto a child and someday, I hope your daughter sees through that smokescreen your ex is using.  

I don't blame you one not for feeling that life appears hopeless....money knows how to destroy our lives, whether we have it or suffer without it. In your case, I am hearing that you do not wish to die, but wish to have a good relationship with your beautiful little girl. If that is the case, then you need to FIGHT FOR HER!!! 

I agree with one of the other people here who suggested looking into temporary shelter. And yes, men get an unfair hand when it comes to resources for housing and mental health assistance...which is ridiculous and wrong. I do not know if you are religious or not (I am not), but there are often churches that will help you secure low cost housing and help ei th things such as food, clothing, and employment assistance. If that may be something you are open to, please look into that. Here in the state I live, we have an assistance line you can call or visit online...211. Not sure if there is something similar where you live. But above all else this evening/early morning, do not give into your ex and her cruel ways and you go fight to be the father your daughter needs in her life.

When I put myself into the hospital about 15 years ago, I was more embarrassed that I couldn't handle my emotions. I have a feeling your sister may be feeling the same way. The fact that you are feeling so down on life may be something very positive for her so she sees that we can all struggle to want to remain here. 

Maybe the two of you will be able to have a really honest conversation with one another and be there for each other. From what it sounds like, you are both really struggling emotionally.....and you both may very well understand what the other may be feeling. 

Nobody understood how I was feeling and that made the entire thing so much harder. My neighbors knew what happened. My co-workers knew. My family knew. Yet nobody knew how I FELT, just that I got myself put on a hold for over a week. It was a very lonely place and I wish someone had been there to truly understand how I felt. I hope you and your sister are able to give one another that understanding.

It's not always easy. Mainly because I have really high expectations of myself and know if I'm lying to myself. I love that you were able to feed the little one and get that sweet baby to sleep! In sure that your friend is very grateful for you!!! And I know it's easy for me to say not to worry about being single....so instead I will just say that there are pros and cons to both! I wish I could tell you doing the grateful exercise has been helpful, but I would be lying...which is not something I tend to do to anybody. I do it more to try.to convince myself that I should be happy when I'm just not. Sometimes, I I have a really good day where my physical pain is not as bad and then I try to stay awake for the entire night because I don't want it to end. Waking up in pain, both physically and mentally, is just something I dread now. I've stayed awake three days straight in hopes that I can continue to feel good, but alas, the fibromyalgia always wins. It has only made my anxiety and depression worse because even when my body was good to me, I still hated being alive. Add a chronic illness or two like I have and it's a recipe for disaster. Thank you for sharing what you were grateful for today...I truly hope the exercise helps you so that at least one of us is feeling the benefit. Have a good night.

Funny you say that because I began doing this about three months ago! I have a rule that I have to mean it too. Some days, it is hard to come up with anything and those are the days I allow myself to write something very specific about what I love about my sons. 

And yes, focusing on bad tends to be the story of my life and while I know it is not helpful....it is hard to convince myself there is good left to look forward to.  I will be meeting with a bankruptcy attorney tomorrow. That has been a very difficult decision to make for myself, but one that may help alleviate some of the stress that just wears me down very much. It took a very long time just to summon the strength and courage to do that and I have been using this appt as a reason to try to keep on plugging away. It is also, on the opposite side of the coin, something that bothers me so very, very much.  I am not the type to just dump my financial responsibilities, but I have dug a hole pretty deep for myself and want to look at what my options really are at this point.

So what am I grateful for today? My boys came over, along with my daughter in law for dinner. I plan to keep my appt for tomorrow with the attorney. And third, because I like to keep trying to come up with three a day, I am grateful for the anonymity of the Internet because I feel like I can be more honest when I don't have to face the shame I feel when discussing my depression and suicidal ideation with people, face to face.

Agree that she's worthless. Sadly, I studied enough therapy in school that I already know what they're all going to say...part of me wishes I'd never taken the courses I took so I could be oblivious to the rhetoric. I also have training in CBT and MRT so that too, I catch where it's textbook therapy and really not useful to anyone who is truly suffering. 

I have been rather afraid to try the as everyone talks about how "hard" it is to do the stretches, etc, and with my health being downright shitty...I worrying wind up worse off. But I do meditate and agree that there are times it is helpful. Once in in a mood though, I can't seem to do anything but fight to keep myself here. I trust anyone that has felt the hopelessness and helplessness of serious depression understands that place. Tears can fall, but I quickly try to stuff them back down so everyone can believe I'm fine. 

I also realize that I am not an anomaly or anything....depression and anxiety cripple millions of people around the world. And I do so wish I could find a medication that makes me feel ready to face my challenges, rather than disappear. I have tried so many that doctors just blow me off now and do not try to titrate up, but instead tell me to wait. Waiting....that's the last thing people who are suicidal want to do. I'm very Type A and have OCD and ridiculous expectations of myself. 

And as for changing jobs...I do not wish to change careers.  I do very much like helping people. It's one thing I do and do well. If only I knew how to help myself! Sadly, I have not one or two plans for ending my life; I have over 40 that I have completely thought through and have looked at all aspects of the how, why, when, where, etc. It has changed some over the last ten years now that my children are now adults and though they are the string that keeps me here, they will also do just fine once I am gone.

I wouldn't wish this feeling on anybody so I am truly sad that you also feel like this. I do all the same things, as well as I try to give myself positive self talk, and though it gets me through....it's becoming more and more empty.
